title: Use binary search
text: For a number in an ordered range, binary search can find it efficiently: each higher-or-lower clue should eliminate about half of the remaining candidates.

title: Narrow the range after Too High
text: After a Too High result, the secret must be below that guess. Lower the upper end of your possible range to one less than the guess, then choose only within the smaller range.

title: Narrow the range after Too Low
text: After a Too Low result, the secret must be above that guess. Raise the lower end of your possible range to one more than the guess, then choose only within the smaller range.

title: Choose the midpoint
text: When both ends of your possible range are known, try its midpoint. This balances the remaining choices and is the key step in binary search.

title: Avoid repeated guesses
text: Do not guess a number you have already tried. Keep track of previous guesses and use each higher-or-lower result to remove impossible numbers from consideration.

title: Easy difficulty tip
text: On Easy, the range is small, so keep a compact lower and upper bound and adjust the midpoint after each clue. You have enough attempts to refine the range steadily.

title: Normal difficulty tip
text: On Normal, use the lower and upper bounds carefully and make large, balanced cuts. A midpoint strategy helps you use the available attempts efficiently.

title: Hard difficulty tip
text: On Hard, attempts are limited, so avoid small incremental guesses. Start near the midpoint and use every Too High or Too Low clue to cut the remaining range substantially.
